en: Six bodhisattvas should also recite and uphold this sutra:

Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrīḍita (Lion’s Play), Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrānta (Lion’s Valiant Stride), and Bodhisattva Siṃhadhvaja (Lion’s Banner). [These were translated during the Later Han period; their translators are lost and they are appended here.]
The Bodhisattva Siṃhakāra, the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhavīryavikrama, and the Bodhisattva Vajramativighaṭana.
Lofty are the Buddhas of the ten directions; majestic are the Kings among Sages.
They possess the thirty-two marks of excellence and the eighty minor characteristics.
From his body issues forth wondrous radiance, Universally illuminating all the ten directions.
I vow that my very self shall take refuge, Bowing my head to all the Kings of Dharma.
The sublime Buddhas of the ten directions, Possessing infinite great compassion.
Having established the various great vows to deliver all sentient beings,
those who hear much and rejoice possess merits beyond measure;
may I take refuge in their very persons and bow my head to these Great Compassionate Ones.
Majestic are the Buddhas of the ten directions, Their merit and virtue are immeasurable;
Their wisdom is like a boundless ocean, Irrigating and nourishing all the ten directions.
Whoever hears their name Shall have their faults removed and all calamities dispelled.
I take refuge in Great Wisdom; I bow my head to the King of Perfect Enlightenment.
Sublime are the Buddhas of the ten directions, whose lands are exceedingly pure, adorned with the seven treasures, and possessing the form of exquisite sandalwood fragrance.
All are exclusively bodhisattvas, and even the name of the two vehicles does not exist;
they teach only the excellence of the path of prajñā for those who do not regress.
Lofty are the Buddhas of the ten directions, the jewels of the Way throughout the three periods of time.
Those who hear, believe, and rejoice in this shall swiftly achieve unsurpassed truth;
Wandering upon the bodhisattva path, they will firmly abide in non-retrogression.
In every birth they shall always see the Buddhas, And quickly encounter all the World-Honored Ones.
The towering Buddhas of the ten directions, The guides of the three periods of time—
With a sincere heart harboring reverence, Believing with joy and free from doubt,
One’s birth shall always be upright and noble, And one’s countenance will be exceedingly radiant.
"Your eloquence and wisdom are uniquely profound; I pray you, pay homage to the Teacher of Gods and Humans.
Separately, there were four other bodhisattvas—these four great beings were all the teachers of the Buddhas of the ten directions in the past.
When these four great beings first began their practice, they made this great vow, saying:
"I shall deliver all sentient beings; only when they have all attained nirvana will I then attain Buddhahood."
For this reason, one should recite, chant, and uphold [these names], thereby attaining immeasurable and boundless merit until reaching the stage of non-retrogression.
Suppose the entire void of the trichiliocosm were filled with purple-polished gold, which one were to give away as a gift;

it would not equal the merit obtained by reciting the names of these four great beings for even a single moment. The merit so gained exceeds that of the gift of all that gold by thousands of billions of times.
Their names are:
Bodhisattva Abandoning the Shroud of Defilements, Bodhisattva Tranquil Faculties, Bodhisattva Wisdom Splendor, and Bodhisattva Non-Departure.
These six bodhisattvas shall also recite and uphold this sutra.
